verdict.rationale: cubic lets teams define custom review rules (custom agents) in `cubic.yaml`, and these run automatically when new pull requests open. It also offers configurable automatic actions such as auto-approval under repository policy and automatic thread resolution when an issue is fixed. However, these are fixed, PR-review-scoped behaviors rather than a general rule engine that maps arbitrary events to arbitrary actions. Missing for 10: user-defined event→action rules beyond PR review, documentation of a selectable range of trigger events and action types, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Custom agents are review rules that enforce your organization's specific best practices across pull requests.
`cubic.yaml` lives in the root of your repository and becomes the source of truth for AI review behavior, ignore patterns, PR descriptions, and custom agents.
cubic automatically starts reviewing new pull requests in your selected repositories.
cubic can approve clean pull requests automatically when your repository policy allows it.
Enable automatic thread resolution to close findings when the issue is fixed
